title: 2026-09-08-poc-weekly-bootstrap-orchestration-and-staging-gate

Action items: Redwood to share gated checklist and secure upload link, BlueArc to provision KMS key and SSO test user, schedule security deep-dive next week.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-08 15:00 PDT | Duration 58m | Attendees Jordan, Maya, Liam (Redwood) / Samantha, Rajesh, Ellen, Tom (BlueArc)

00:00 Jordan: okay folks, uh good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight 45 to 60 minutes, aim to leave clear next steps. quick roll call?
00:10 Samantha: hey all, Samantha here, thanks Jordan.
00:12 Rajesh: Rajesh on infra.
:14 Ellen: Ellen, security.
00:16 Tom: Tom product.
00:18 Jordan: great, maya from our side?
00:20 Maya: hi, maya here, i'll lead the bench triage.
00:23 Jordan: quick agenda - access status, bench results you saw in the spreadsheet, kv cache/latency questions, kms/ss0 (i mean sso) and k m s integration, then canary plan and next steps.
00:34 Samantha: sounds good.

00:45 Jordan: Rajesh, can you start with access? last week we asked for the peering bits and an S3 upload role so we can pull your dataset and run the warmup. where are we?
01:02 Rajesh: yeah, so peering is mostly done, we had a hiccup with CIDR overlaps, fixed that. the firewall rule we didnt open for the control plane's health checks cause we were conservative, so open request is in but pending approval from network ops. we can manually add Redwood IPs if you give us the list, or we can have a jumpbox.
01:21 Jordan: we'll paste the IP ranges in the doc after this call, should be the low-friction path. also need the STS role for the S3 read.
01:30 Rajesh: working on the IAM role, should be live tomorrow.

01:45 Maya: quick note on creds - for KV cache profiling we need token-level traces for a few warmup sessions, please don't use prod keys for that, we recommend a scoped pilot token.
02:00 Ellen: that's fine but from security side we need token rotation and audit logs enabled. we also need to understand where logs land and retention period -- health care regs for us.
02:14 Jordan: totally. we have audit logs shipped to a customer-controlled s3 bucket by default and you can set retention. i'll include the doc link in the followup.
02:24 Samantha: also need data residency clarification - the pilot should keep embeddings and logs in us-east-1.
02:30 Maya: our dedicated pilot nodes can be pinned to region, we'll make sure the runtime and cache remain in us-east-1.

03:00 Jordan: okay onto the benchmark spreadsheet - Maya you ran the first two runs last night and saw an uptick in tail latency?
03:12 Maya: yeah, so we ran three profiles: short chat (avg 64 tokens), doc summarize (avg 512 tokens), and rerank. normal for the first two, but the doc summarize had a 99th percentile spike to ~1.3s per token which is higher than expected for the GPU profile we selected. a few possible causes: kv cache misses during chunked requests, suboptimal kernel selection for long seq length, or our batching threshold kicking in unexpectedly.
03:41 Rajesh: do you think it's network related? we saw a few retries on TCP near the same window.
03:47 Maya: maybe, but the profiler shows GPU stalls aligned with cache population. there's also a JVM-ish process on the customer side warming up that caused bursty traffic, that might have impacted concurrency.
04:05 Samantha: hmm, the doc summarization job is run as a backend batch that pipes in chunks, might be sending overlapping prefixes. we can throttle.
04:12 Maya: if you can reduce concurrency and let us re-run the long-tail profile that would help isolate the cache miss hypothesis.
04:20 Jordan: action: lower concurrency for the doc summarize run, rerun tomorrow morning, maya will compare logs.

04:40 Maya: also flag - we saw a difference between the quantization profile you selected and the runtime default. if you stick to 8-bit quant on that model variant we saw a small quality delta but better latency; if quality is paramount we can keep 16-bit and tune batch sizes.
05:01 Tom: for BlueArc product the quality threshold is strict on summarization - a 2% ROUGE drop is concerning. can you surface a pairwise comparison?
05:10 Maya: yes i'll generate a diff on the prompt set.

05:30 Ellen: quick security question - KMS ownership, we want customer-managed keys (CMK) for PHI. what's the flow?
05:41 Jordan: support both; for private deployments you bring the KMS/HSM and we integrate via ARN and grant access. for hosted pilot we can accept a customer-managed key in your cloud account and encrypt logs/encryption at rest. we'll need an IAM role- assume pattern and a couple of grants.
05:58 Ellen: will you require cross-account roles? we prefer to keep keys within our account, no cross-account key copies.
06:05 Maya: we don't copy keys, we use envelope encryption where Redwood encrypts with a data key that is itself encrypted by your CMK; the unencrypted data key never leaves our host memory.
06:22 Ellen: okay and audit logs for key usage?
06:25 Jordan: yes, key usage events are surfaced in the audit logs; we'll show an example.

06:40 Rajesh: about SSO, we gave you a SAML metadata file and a test user, any issues?
06:47 Jordan: we got the file, the initial handshake succeeded but we couldn't map groups to roles because the assertion name mapping was slightly different - "employeeType" vs our expected "roles" claim.
06:58 Maya: easy fix, Rajesh if you can add a roles claim mapping to the assertion we'll accept it. or we can accept a transform rule in the Console.
07:10 Rajesh: i'll add the claim.

07:20 Jordan: back to canary - recommended plan is 1 hour window at 10% traffic, synthetic load + real minimal traffic, with immediate rollback on 95th percentile latency breach or quality regression. thoughts?
07:36 Tom: 10% is good for us but we need to prove failure modes - if latency doubles we need fallback to local CPU pipeline.
07:43 Maya: Redwood can configure automatic fallback to a smaller on-prem model variant or switch traffic to dedicated pool. fallback policy is configurable per route.
07:56 Samantha: what's the instrumentation look like during canary? token-level traces? cost per token?
08:03 Liam: console will show per-route token counts, latency p95/p99, KV cache hit rate, and an alert stream. we'll also provide a lightweight flame graph on request.
08:12 Samantha: perfect.

08:30 Maya: small gotcha we found: if you set batch size too aggressively with long sequences, it can increase tail latency because of outlier long context. our suggestion: dynamic batching with an aggressive cap for doc-summarize route.
08:46 Rajesh: what's the default cap?
08:48 Maya: default cap is 16 for this runtime, but for 512-token summaries we recommend cap 6-8 to keep latency stable.
08:56 Samantha: ok we'll apply that in the route config.

09:10 Ellen: about compliance docs - can you share SOC2 cert and your ISO mapping?
09:16 Jordan: yes i'll include SOC2 type II, the ISO mapping worksheet, and an audit log sample; will put in secure link.
09:24 Ellen: we also need a list of sub-processors and where logs are stored.
09:29 Jordan: will include sub-processor list and storage locations; default is customer-chosen region but we can detail backups.

09:45 Maya: one more note on KV cache - turn on prefix caching for the summarize route, that cut cost 15% in our internal tests. but that requires consistent prompt templates; if you vary prefixes a lot the cache hit rate will be low.
09:58 Tom: our prompts vary per customer record but we can standardize a three-step template for initial pilot - that'll help.
10:06 Rajesh: we'll standardize.

10:20 Jordan: any blockers left that would prevent the canary 9/15?
10:23 Samantha: KMS key still needs to be provisioned and network ops needs to approve firewall change, both in flight.
10:31 Rajesh: firewall approval likely by 9/10.
10:34 Ellen: KMS done once I finish the IAM doc updates, aiming 9/11.

10:45 Jordan: cool, so recap - Redwood sends onboarding checklist + secure links, Maya sends benchmark scripts and diff, BlueArc provisions KMS and updates SAML roles, then we schedule security deep dive 9/14 and run canary 9/15.
10:58 Samantha: good.

11:05 Jordan: any final Qs?
11:08 Rajesh: one quick ask - can we get a small runbook for rollback steps during canary? if it hits our SLOs we want automated rollback into local fallback.
11:18 Maya: yes i'll drop a runbook in the shared folder, includes API calls, console switches, and default thresholds.
11:25 Jordan: great. thanks everyone, will follow up with the notes and links.
11:30 Tom: thanks.
11:32 Ellen: thanks all.

End of transcript.
